The '''2019–20 [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] season''' was the club's [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|116th season]] in existence and its [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|89th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. It covered a period from 1 July 2019 to 7 August 2020.

This season was the first since [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|2013–14]] without goalkeeper [[Keylor Navas]], who departed for [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]].

==Kits==
'''Supplier:''' [[Adidas]] / '''Sponsor:''' Emirates

==Summary==
===Pre-season===
[[File:FC RB Salzburg v.Real Madrid (Testspiel, 7. August 2019) 21.jpg|thumb|right|310px|Madrid players in a pre-season friendly against [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]]]]
On 4 June, [[Luka Jović]] signed from [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] on a contract until 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eintracht.de/en/news/article/luka-jovic-signs-for-real-madrid-73376/|title=Luka Jovic signs for Real Madrid|publisher=eintracht.de|date=4 June 2019|access-date=5 July 2019|archive-date=4 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190604181449/https://www.eintracht.de/en/news/article/luka-jovic-signs-for-real-madrid-73376/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Three days later [[Eden Hazard]] was acquired from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/06/07/eden-hazard-transfer-deal-agreed|title=Eden Hazard transfer deal agreed|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=7 June 2019|access-date=7 June 2019}}</ref> while [[Ferland Mendy]] was bought from [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on a six-year contract on 12 June.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/articles/2019/06/12/ferland-mendy-completes-move-real-madrid|title=Ferland Mendy completes move to Real Madrid|publisher=ol.fr|date=12 June 2019}}</ref> On 20 June, [[Marcos Llorente]] was sold to [[Atlético Madrid]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/06/official-announcement-marcos-llorente|title=Official Announcement: Marcos Llorente|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=20 June 2019|access-date=20 June 2019}}</ref> and [[Mateo Kovačić]] joined [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on 1 July, having spent the previous season there on loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/07/official-announcement-kovacic|title=Official Announcement: Kovacic|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=1 July 2019|access-date=1 July 2019}}</ref>

===August===
The first match of the season, on 17 August 2019, saw a 3–1 victory for Madrid at [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]]. The goals came from [[Karim Benzema]], [[Toni Kroos]] and [[Lucas Vázquez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/08/1-3-real-madrid-start-laliga-with-a-great-win-at-balaidos|title=1–3: Real Madrid start LaLiga with a great win at Balaídos|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=17 August 2019|access-date=17 August 2019}}</ref> A week later, the game against [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] ended in a 1–1 draw after Benzema initially gave Real the lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/08/1-1-real-madrid-miss-out-on-the-win-in-the-dying-minutes|title=1–1: Real Madrid miss out on the win in the dying minutes|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=24 August 2019|access-date=24 August 2019}}</ref>

===September===
On the first day of the month, [[Gareth Bale]] secured one point for Real in a 2–2 draw, after he equalized the game twice at [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/2-2-draw-in-villarreal-with-a-bale-brace|title=2–2: Draw in Villarreal with a Bale brace|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=1 September 2019|access-date=1 September 2019}}</ref> A day later, [[Keylor Navas]] left Madrid to join [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], with [[Alphonse Areola]] replacing him on a one-year loan deal from the Parisians.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/official-announcement-keylor-navas|title=Official Announcement: Keylor Navas|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=2 September 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/areola-becomes-a-real-madrid-player|title=Areola becomes a Real Madrid player|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=2 September 2019|access-date=27 June 2022}}</ref> On 14 September, a brace from Benzema and a goal from [[Casemiro]] gave Madrid a 3–0 lead, before [[Levante UD|Levante]] was able to cut it to 3–2, which was the final result.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/3-2-benzema-at-the-double-in-victory-over-levante|title=3–2: Benzema at the double in victory over Levante|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=14 September 2019|access-date=14 September 2019}}</ref> In the new [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] season, Madrid started with a 0–3 loss at Paris on 18 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/3-0-madrid-lose-in-paris|title=3–0: Madrid lose in Paris|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=18 September 2019|access-date=18 September 2019}}</ref> Another goal from Benzema lifted Madrid to a 1–0 win at [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] on 22 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/0-1-a-win-at-the-pizjuan-thanks-to-a-goal-from-benzema|title=0–1: A win at the Pizjuán thanks to a goal from Benzema|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 September 2019|access-date=22 September 2019}}</ref> Three days later, goals from [[Vinícius Júnior]] and [[Rodrygo]] secured a 2–0 home win over [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], putting Madrid at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/2-0-goals-from-vinicius-jr-and-rodrygo-see-real-madrid-go-top|title=2–0: Goals from Vinicius Jr. and Rodrygo see Real Madrid go top|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=25 September 2019|access-date=25 September 2019}}</ref> The [[Madrid derby]] on 28 September ended in a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/0-0-madrid-remain-top-of-the-table-after-metropolitano-clash|title=0–0: Madrid remain top of the table after Metropolitano clash|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=28 September 2019|access-date=28 September 2019}}</ref>

===October===
On the first day of the month, Madrid took on [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] in the Champions League. The game ended in a 2–2 draw, after [[Sergio Ramos]] and Casemiro brought Madrid back from a 0–2 deficit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/2-2-real-madrid-claim-draw-against-brugge|title=2–2: Real Madrid claim draw against Brugge|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=1 October 2019|access-date=1 October 2019}}</ref> Four days later, Real defeated [[Granada CF|Granada]] 4–2 with goals from Benzema, Hazard, [[Luka Modrić]] and [[James Rodríguez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/05/4-2-real-madrid-top-the-table-going-into-the-international-break|title=4–2: Real Madrid top the table going into the international break|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=5 October 2019|access-date=5 October 2019}}</ref> On 19 October, the away game at [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] was lost 0–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/19/1-0-defeat-at-son-moix|title=1–0: Defeat at Son Moix|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=19 October 2019|access-date=19 October 2019}}</ref> The Champions League match at [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] was won 1–0 after a goal from Kroos.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/22/0-1-important-win-in-istanbul|title=0–1: Important win in Istanbul|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 October 2019|access-date=22 October 2019}}</ref> On 30 October, the match against [[CD Leganés]] was won 5–0 with goals from Rodrygo, Kroos, [[Sergio Ramos]], Benzema and Jović.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/30/5-0-real-madrid-steamroller-leganes|title=5–0: Real Madrid steamroller Leganés|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=30 October 2019|access-date=30 October 2019}}</ref>

===November===
On 2 November, the game against [[Real Betis]] ended in a 0–0 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/02/0-0-all-square-after-a-controversial-refereeing-decision|title=0–0: All square after a controversial refereeing decision|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=2 November 2019|access-date=2 November 2019}}</ref> The game against Galatasaray in the Champions League was won 6–0 after a hat-trick from Rodrygo, a brace from Benzema and a goal from Ramos.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/06/6-0-rodrygo-hat-trick-brings-the-whites-closer-to-the-last-16|title=6–0: Rodrygo 'Hat-trick' brings the Whites closer to the last-16|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=6 November 2019|access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref> Three days later, the away game at [[SD Eibar]] was won 4–0 with a brace from Benzema and goals from Ramos and Valverde.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/09/0-4-the-goals-flow-in-a-footballing-exhibition|title=0–4: The goals flow in a footballing exhibition|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=9 November 2019|access-date=9 November 2019}}</ref> After the international break, Madrid recorded a 3–1 victory over [[Real Sociedad]] on 23 November. After falling behind early, goals from Benzema, Valverde and Modrić secured the three points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/23/3-1-real-madrid-come-from-behind-to-clinch-three-big-points-in-fight-for-laliga|title=3–1: Real Madrid come from behind to clinch three big points in fight for LaLiga|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=23 November 2019|access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> Three days later, the Champions league match against Paris ended in a 2–2 draw, with a brace from Benzema initially putting Real up 2–0 only for Paris to score two successive goals late in the game. With that draw, Madrid advanced to the knockout stage of the tournament for the 23rd time in a row.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/26/2-2-benzema-at-double-as-madrid-advance-to-champions-league-last-16|title=2–2: Benzema at double as Madrid advance to Champions League last 16|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=26 November 2019|access-date=26 November 2019}}</ref> On the last day of the month, goals from Ramos and [[Dani Carvajal]] got Madrid a 2–1 win at [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/30/1-2-mendizorroza-victory-secures-top-spot|title=1–2: Mendizorroza victory secures top spot|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=30 November 2019|access-date=30 November 2019}}</ref>

===December===
The game against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] on 7 December ended in a 2–0 win after [[Raphaël Varane]] and Benzema scored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/07/2-0-varane-y-benzema-strike-to-send-madrid-top|title=2–0: Varane & Benzema strike to send Madrid top|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=7 December 2019|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> Four days later, the last Champions League group stage game at Brugge was won 3–1, with Rodrygo, Vinícius and Modrić scoring the goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/11/1-3-victory-in-bruges-to-close-out-the-group-stage|title=1–3: Victory in Bruges to close out the Group Stage|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=11 December 2019|access-date=11 December 2019}}</ref> A late goal from Benzema saved Madrid one point in a 1–1 draw at [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 15 December.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/15/1-1-real-madrid-equalise-in-the-dying-seconds-at-mestalla|title=1–1: Real Madrid equalise in the dying seconds at Mestalla|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=15 December 2019|access-date=15 December 2019}}</ref> The season's first ''[[El Clásico|Clásico]]'' against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on 18 December resulted in a 0–0 stalemate, with Madrid thoroughly outplaying Barça away from home but failing to convert.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/18/0-0-real-madrid-deserved-to-win-el-clasico|title=0–0: Real Madrid deserved to win el Clásico|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=18 December 2019|access-date=18 December 2019}}</ref> Four days later, the last game of the year against [[Athletic Bilbao]] also ended 0–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/22/0-0-the-woodwork-denies-real-madrid-the-win|title=0–0: The woodwork denies Real Madrid the win|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 December 2019|access-date=22 December 2019}}</ref>

===January===
The new year started with a 3–0 victory against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on 4 January. The goals were scored by Varane and Modrić plus an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/04/0-3-real-madrid-kick-off-2020-with-a-win-in-getafe|title=0–3: Real Madrid kick off 2020 with a win in Getafe|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=4 January 2020|access-date=4 January 2020}}</ref> Four days later, Valencia was defeated 3–1 in the semi-final of the [[2019–20 Supercopa de España]] after goals from Kroos, [[Isco]] and Modrić.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/08/1-3-madrid-book-their-place-in-the-spanish-super-cup-final|title=1–3: Madrid book their place in the Spanish Super Cup final|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=8 January 2020|access-date=8 January 2020}}</ref> On 12 January, the Supercopa was won 4–1 in a penalty shootout against Atlético Madrid, with the match itself having ended in a 0–0 draw. This marked the eleventh time that Madrid won the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/12/0-0-eleventh-spanish-super-cup|title=0–0 (4–1): Eleventh Spanish Super Cup!|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=12 January 2020|access-date=12 January 2020}}</ref> Next, a brace from Casemiro secured three points for Real in a 2–1 victory over Sevilla.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/18/2-1-a-casemiro-double-temporarily-sends-madrid-top|title=2–1: A Casemiro double temporarily sends Madrid top|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=18 January 2020|access-date=18 January 2020}}</ref> [[Reinier Jesus Carvalho]] joined Madrid on 20 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flamengo.com.br/noticias/futebol/nota-oficial---reinier-|title=Nota oficial – Reinier|publisher=flamengo.com.br|date=20 January 2020|access-date=20 January 2020}}</ref> Two days later, in the round of 32 of the [[2019–20 Copa del Rey]], Madrid defeated [[Unionistas de Salamanca CF]] 3–1 with goals from Bale, [[Brahim Díaz]] and an own goal to advance to the next round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/22/1-3-madrid-book-their-copa-del-rey-last-sixteen-spot|title=1–3: Madrid book their Copa del Rey last-sixteen spot|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 January 2020|access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref> In the last league game for this month, Madrid beat Valladolid 1–0 at the [[Estadio José Zorrilla|José Zorrilla Stadium]] to move to the top of the table and establish a three-point lead over Barcelona. The only goal was scored by [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/26/0-1-real-madrid-beat-valladolid-to-go-top-of-the-table|title=0–1: Real Madrid beat Valladolid to go top of the table|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=26 January 2020|access-date=26 January 2020}}</ref> On 29 January, Real defeated [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] 4–0 to proceed to the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey. The goals were scored by Varane, Vázquez, Vinícius and Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/29/0-4-victory-in-zaragoza-sees-the-whites-into-the-copa-quarter-finals|title=0–4: Victory in Zaragoza sees the Whites into the Copa quarter-finals|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=29 January 2020|access-date=29 January 2020}}</ref>

===February===
The first day of the new month brought another Madrid derby against Atlético. Benzema scored the lone goal of the game to give Real a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/01/1-0-the-laliga-leaders-come-out-on-top-in-the-derby|title=1–0: The LaLiga leaders come out on top in the derby|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=1 February 2020|access-date=1 February 2020}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid lost the Copa del Rey quarter-final match to Sociedad 3–4, with [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]], Rodrygo and Nacho scoring the goals in an attempted late comeback. With that result, Madrid's drought in the competition extended to six years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/06/3-4-real-madrid-went-all-out-to-the-end|title=3–4: Real Madrid went all out to the end|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=6 February 2020|access-date=6 February 2020}}</ref> The game against Osasuna on 9 February was won 4–1. Isco, Ramos, Vázquez and Jović scored the goals after Madrid fell behind early.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/09/1-4-the-leaders-come-from-behind-at-el-sadar|title=1–4: The leaders come from behind at El Sadar|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=9 February 2020|access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref> A week later, the game against Celta Vigo ended in a 2–2 draw with a late equalizer, despite Kroos and Ramos giving Real a 2–1 lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/16/2-2-real-madrid-draws-and-stay-top-of-the-league|title=2–2: Real Madrid draws and stay top of the league|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=16 February 2020|access-date=16 February 2020}}</ref> On 22 February, the match against Levante was lost 0–1 due to a late goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/22/1-0-defeat-at-the-ciudad-de-valencia|title=1–0: Defeat at the Ciudad de Valencia|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 February 2020|access-date=22 February 2020}}</ref> The first leg of the Champions League round of 16 against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] was lost 1–2. Isco scored the lone goal for Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/26/1-2-real-madrid-need-to-stage-comeback-in-manchester|title=1–2: Real Madrid need to stage comeback in Manchester|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=26 February 2020|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref>

===March===
On the first day of the month, Real defeated Barcelona 2–0 in the season's second ''Clásico''. Vinícius and [[Mariano Díaz|Mariano]] scored the goals, with Madrid regaining the lead position in the standings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/01/2-0-clasico-win-and-top-spot-for-madrid|title=2–0: Clásico win and top spot for Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=1 March 2020|access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref> A week later, the away game at Betis was lost 1–2, meaning Madrid again slipped to second. Benzema scored the penalty for Real.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/08/2-1-real-madrid-beaten-at-the-villamarin|title=2–1: Real Madrid beaten at the Villamarín|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=8 March 2020|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref> On 12 March, after a [[Trey Thompkins|player]] from Real Madrid's [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|basketball]] team tested positive for [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]], all players of basketball and football teams alike were forced into quarantine. This superseded the postponements of several matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/12/official-announcement|title=Official Announcement|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=12 March 2020|access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref> On 23 March, following the outbreak of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]], the league was suspended indefinitely.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/noticias/acuerdo-comision-seguimiento-del-convenio-coordinacion-rfef-laliga|title=Acuerdo de la Comisión de Seguimiento del Convenio de Coordinación RFEF-LaLiga|publisher=rfef.es|date=23 March 2020|access-date=23 March 2020|archive-date=28 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200528064505/https://www.rfef.es/noticias/acuerdo-comision-seguimiento-del-convenio-coordinacion-rfef-laliga|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===May===
After a two and a half-month hiatus, it was announced on 31 May that the league would be resumed on 11 June, with all games being played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/este-es-el-calendario-de-las-ultimas-jornadas-de-laliga-santander-y-laliga-smartbank|title=Este es el calendario de las últimas jornadas de LaLiga Santander y LaLiga SmartBank|publisher=laliga.com|date=31 May 2020|access-date=31 May 2020}}</ref>

===June===
In Madrid's first game back after the break on 14 June, Eibar was defeated 3–1 with goals from Kroos, Ramos and Marcelo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/14/3-1-a-win-on-the-return-of-laliga|title=3–1: A win on the return of LaLiga|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=14 June 2020|access-date=14 June 2020}}</ref> Four days later, the game against Valencia ended in a 3–0 victory, with a brace from Benzema and a goal from Asensio.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/18/3-0-real-madrid-win-to-keep-the-pressure-on-in-the-laliga-title-race|title=3–0: Real Madrid win to keep the pressure on in the LaLiga title race|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=18 June 2020|access-date=18 June 2020}}</ref> On 21 June, Madrid was able to defeat Real Sociedad by a 2–1 margin, getting back to the top of the table. The goals were scored by Ramos and Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/21/1-2-madrid-win-and-move-top-of-laliga|title=1–2: Madrid win and move top of LaLiga|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=21 June 2020|access-date=21 June 2020}}</ref> Another three days later, Mallorca was defeated 2–0 with goals from Vinícius and Ramos.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/24/2-0-madrid-beat-mallorca-to-stay-top|title=2–0: Madrid beat Mallorca to stay top|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=24 June 2020|access-date=24 June 2020}}</ref> A goal from Casemiro secured another three points for Real, as they defeated Espanyol 1–0 on 28 June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/28/0-1-real-madrid-extend-their-lead-a-the-top|title=0–1: Real Madrid extend their lead at the top|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=28 June 2020|access-date=28 June 2020}}</ref>

===July===
On 2 July, Getafe was defeated 1–0 per a Ramos penalty, which gave Madrid a four-point cushion at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/02/1-0-the-laliga-leaders-win-again-to-open-up-a-4-point-advantage|title=1–0: The LaLiga leaders win again to open up a 4-point advantage|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=2 July 2020|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> The exact same scenario secured Real another victory three days later, against Athletic Bilbao.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/05/0-1-the-laliga-leaders-pick-up-seventh-successive-win-in-bilbao|title=0–1: The LaLiga leaders pick up seventh successive win in Bilbao|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=5 July 2020|access-date=5 July 2020}}</ref> On 10 July, Alavés was defeated 2–0, after Benzema and Asensio scored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/10/2-0-leaders-record-eighth-straight-win|title=2–0: Leaders record eighth straight win|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=10 July 2020|access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref> Two early goals from Mendy and Benzema secured Madrid their ninth win in a row with a 2–1 victory at Granada. After that game, Real had a four-point lead in the standings with two matches to go.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/13/1-2-leaders-secure-ninth-win-on-bounce|title=1–2: Leaders secure ninth win on bounce|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=13 July 2020|access-date=13 July 2020}}</ref> After a narrow 2–1 home victory over Villarreal on 16 July, thanks to a brace from Benzema, Madrid mathematically clinched a record-extending 34th league title. Conversely, this was only their third title since the start of Barcelona's [[La Liga#2010s: Barcelona, Real Madrid and Atletico|dominance]] in the [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/16/2-1-laliga-champions|title=2–1: LaLiga champions!|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=16 July 2020|access-date=16 July 2020}}</ref> Three days later, the last league game of the season at Leganés was drawn 2–2 with goals from Ramos and Asensio.<ref>{{cite web|title=2–2: The LaLiga champions end the season with a draw|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/19/2-2-the-laliga-champions-end-the-season-with-a-draw/amp|work=Alberto Navarro|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=20 July 2020|access-date=3 July 2022}}</ref>

===August===
After the league was finished, Madrid went on to play the postponed second leg of the Champions League against Manchester City on 7 August. The match was a practical repeat of the first leg, with Madrid losing 1–2 and being eliminated 2–4 on aggregate. The lone goal came from Benzema who scored an equalizer in the first half. This result meant that Real had been knocked out in the round of 16 for the second season running.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/08/07/2-1-madrid-bow-out-of-champions-league|title=2–1: Madrid bow out of Champions League|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=7 August 2020|access-date=7 August 2020}}</ref>
